weaknesses: The central claim of smoothly scaling safety with compute is only weakly demonstrated. Across most plots, nearly all improvement occurs when moving from degree 1 to degree 2; degrees 3–5, and even 3–10 in the order ablation, usually plateau or fluctuate. The efficiency evaluation does not substantiate the main practical claim. Cascades are evaluated using summed parameter counts as a compute proxy, exclude the dominant LLM forward pass needed to obtain activations, and are not benchmarked for actual end-to-end latency or throughput. The safety evaluation is too narrow for the deployment claims: it measures only F1 on harmful-prompt classification. It lacks harmful-class recall or false-negative rates at fixed false-positive rates, AUROC/AUPRC, risk-coverage analysis for early exits, cross-dataset or out-of-distribution transfer, adaptive jailbreak attacks, and monitoring of harmful model outputs. Confidence-based exits are particularly risky without robust OOD calibration.

The baseline suite misses important controls. The stated bilinear baseline uses the restrictive positive-semidefinite form z^T A^T A z, whereas the TPC quadratic term permits signed eigencomponents through lambda. A general signed low-rank quadratic classifier, stagewise additive MLP, boosted classifier, or cascade of independently trained probes would better isolate the benefit of polynomial structure and progressive training.

The interpretability claim is substantially overstated. The paper provides one example whose highlighted pair contributions are tiny relative to the total logit, assigns no semantic meaning to the neurons, and evaluates neither stability nor usefulness of the explanations. Overall improvements over strong baselines are often only a few tenths of an F1 point and can overlap the displayed variability. Reproducibility is also limited by the blank code URL and incomplete details about checkpoint selection and timing methodology.

The evaluation does not establish robustness as a deployed safety monitor. TPC is slower than EE-MLP at batch size one, and all examined heads are below roughly 0.1% of the base model size, leaving the practical importance of optimizing this overhead unclear.

Many headline gains over MLP or EE-MLP are only a few tenths of an F1 point, and TPC often ties or loses on BeaverTails. The baselines do not fully isolate the source of the gains. In particular, there is no stage-wise additive/residual MLP trained with the same greedy freezing objective as TPC. The approach is essentially a stagewise additive low-rank polynomial combined with standard early exiting, but it is not compared with boosting, progressively trained additive MLPs, or cascades of independently trained classifiers. Moreover, TPC receives degree-wise frozen training while EE-MLP is jointly trained, and the bilinear baseline uses the restrictive positive-semidefinite form z^T A^T A z rather than a signed low-rank quadratic comparable to TPC's coefficients.

The overall gains are small and inconsistently favorable. In Table 1, improvements over the strongest baseline on WildGuardMix are generally only a few tenths of an F1 point, TPC loses one comparison, and it trails EE-MLP on three of four BeaverTails models. No confidence intervals or significance tests accompany the table, while the full cascade comparison in the appendix uses only one seed.

The interpretability claims are overstated. Raw-neuron interaction decompositions are basis-dependent, dense, and affected by non-identifiability of the CP factorization. The single example assigns tiny pairwise contributions relative to the total logit and provides no semantic interpretation, stability analysis, or evidence that the explanation helps auditing.

The scope remains narrow for a safety claim: there is no adaptive attack evaluation, jailbreak-success analysis, multi-turn setting, harmful-output monitoring, or demographic error analysis. Comparisons with external monitors are also not controlled because those systems are neither fine-tuned nor carefully prompt-optimized, while the ethics discussion largely overlooks false assurances, disparate false positives, and adversarial adaptation.
